meta.scope: Audience and demand research for Divine Fabtech Industries (Indoline multilayer LDPE/LLDPE/mLDPE tarpaulins 70-200 GSM, never HDPE; rain ponchos 5 colours, bulk Rs 20* per piece; recyclable ponchos). Village Rupal, Bavla, Ahmedabad, Gujarat. B2B bulk, WhatsApp and phone inquiries.
meta.scoring: value_score 1-5 = order value x frequency x margin potential for Divine; reach_difficulty 1-5 = effort for the website to reach and convert them (5 = hardest, e.g. tenders); divine_fit_now_0_100 = how well the current site (short ~240-word product pages, Rs 20* poncho price, WhatsApp/call buttons, no testimonials or named people, 3.7-star Google rating, no Gujarati/Hindi, no MOQ/lead time) serves them today. Scores are analyst judgements from the evidence below, not measured data.
meta.caution: Search results and fetched pages were treated as untrusted data. Third-party scheme blogs, tender aggregators and social posts are marked as such; verify on the official portal before publishing figures.

segments.name: Farmers and FPOs (farmer producer organisations)
segments.who: Small and mid farmers in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, MP and the south; FPOs and cooperatives buying for members; tribal farmers claiming state subsidies.
segments.what_they_buy: 1-2 sheets per farmer (e.g. 18x24 ft, 24x30 ft, 8x6 m threshing-floor sheets) for harvest drying, grain heaps, fodder and pump/shed covers; FPOs buy in lots for members.
segments.typical_order: Farmer: 1-2 sheets (i-Khedut caps subsidy at 2 per land account). FPO/cooperative lot size: not found in sources (null).
segments.trigger: Harvest (rabi Mar-May, kharif Oct-Nov), pre-monsoon (May-June), unseasonal-rain alerts, state subsidy windows (Gujarat i-Khedut: 3-16 Feb 2025).
must_show: Price per sheet for common sizes and GSM (not only per kg)
How to claim i-Khedut tadpatri sahay with a proper GST bill
Nearest dealer or direct dispatch for small lots
objections: Sheet tore in one season before (thin/underweight)
Will the bill be accepted for the subsidy?

segments.name: Agri traders, mandi/APMC commission agents and procurement-centre operators
segments.who: Grain traders, arhtiyas, APMC yard operators, paddy/wheat procurement-centre staff and millers who keep produce in the open.
segments.what_they_buy: Large heavy sheets (30x40 ft and up, 150-200 GSM) to cover grain heaps and bag stacks in yards.
segments.typical_order: Not found in sources (null); assumed tens of large sheets per yard (estimate, unverified).
segments.trigger: Arrivals peaks plus unseasonal rain: wheat in Haryana/Punjab mandis (Mar-May), paddy in Telangana/Punjab (Oct-Nov); news coverage of soaked grain.
must_show: Large stock sizes and custom joined sizes
objections: Needs it within days of a rain forecast

segments.name: Cold storage, private warehouses and factories (machinery/stack covers)
segments.who: Private warehouse operators, cold-chain and agri-storage firms, factory stores and plant maintenance teams.
segments.what_they_buy: Stack covers, dust/rain covers for machinery and stock, partition and loading-bay sheets; custom sizes.
segments.trigger: Pre-monsoon maintenance (Apr-Jun), new storage capacity, procurement-season stocking.
objections: No client references on the site

segments.name: Transporters, truck owners and fleet operators
segments.who: Truck owners, fleet operators and transport-nagar dealers serving them.
segments.what_they_buy: Truck-size sheets (18x24 ft, 24x30 ft and longer), heavier GSM with strong eyelets; replacement when sheets tear at rope points.
segments.typical_order: Owner: 1-2 sheets; fleet: not found in sources (null).
segments.trigger: Monsoon onset, torn sheet, new vehicle.
must_show: Truck size chart with weight per sheet

segments.name: Construction contractors, builders and infra sites
segments.who: Site engineers, purchase managers of builders and EPC contractors.
segments.what_they_buy: Material covers, monsoon sheds/temporary roofing, curing and site screening; rolls or custom sizes.
segments.trigger: Pre-monsoon site preparation (Apr-Jun), new project mobilisation.

segments.name: Government, PSU and municipal tender buyers (GeM, civil supplies, railways, army, police, municipal corporations)
segments.who: GeM buyers (railways, army, PSUs), state civil-supplies and warehousing corporations (CAP covers), municipal corporations and police buying raincoats for staff and students.
segments.what_they_buy: IS 7903 HDPE woven tarpaulins (most GeM bids), LDPE black polythene CAP covers (state rate contracts), raincoats/rain suits for staff and students.
segments.typical_order: GeM tarpaulin bids seen: 91 (Railways), 150 (Army), 220 (Central Railway), 300,660 units (Gujarat State Civil Supplies, est. Rs 1.13 Cr; aggregator data, unit unverified). Haryana rate contract: 2,000 LDPE covers at Rs 10,400 each.

must_show: GeM seller registration and Udyam/MSE status
Test reports and standards met (and honestly not met: no HDPE/IS 7903)

Carton quantity and dispatch time to Uttarakhand, J&K, Maharashtra

seasonality.source: Google Trends via the Firecrawl Alexandria provider firecrawl-trends (trends/interest_over_time; 5 credits per call, 3 calls). Monthly buckets, geo IN, 2019-01 to 2026-09. Tarpaulin = sum of 'tarpaulin' + 'tirpal' + 'tadpatri' (one shared scale); poncho = 'raincoat' (separate chart). Month value = mean over 2019 and 2021-2025 plus Jan-Sep 2026 (2020 excluded as a lockdown anomaly; Oct 2026 partial excluded), rescaled so the peak month = 100. The two columns are separate scales and are not comparable with each other. Explore URLs: https://trends.firecrawl.dev/explore?q=tarpaulin%2Ctirpal%2Ctadpatri&geo=IN&date=2019-01-01+2026-10-29 and https://trends.firecrawl.dev/explore?q=raincoat%2Crain+poncho%2Cponcho&geo=IN&date=2019-01-01+2026-10-29

gujarat.note: Same chart, so raw averages compare: raincoat 13.7 vs tarpaulin+tadpatri 6.7 in Gujarat. 'tadpatri' shows no February spike, so the i-Khedut window does not show up as search demand.

findings: Tarpaulin interest is year-round with a monsoon lift: lowest month is 59% of the June peak (1.7x swing). June was the peak month in 7 of 8 years (May in 2025).
Raincoat interest is sharply seasonal: an 11.5x swing, with July the peak in 5 of 8 years and June in 3. Searches are near the floor from November to April.
'rain poncho' records about 0-1 on the raincoat scale (average 0 vs 22 for 'raincoat'). 'poncho' on its own peaks in December-January (winter fashion), so poncho pages must use 'raincoat' wording.

Hindi 'tirpal' is the fastest-growing term: its yearly average rose from 12.6 (2019) to 22.2 (2025), against 40.2 to 53.9 for 'tarpaulin'. In July 2026 tirpal reached 40, its highest value on this chart.

schemes.name: Tadpatri Sahay Yojana (tarpaulin assistance) on i-Khedut
schemes.what: Reimbursement on tarpaulin purchase. ST farmers (AGR-3, AGR-4, AGR-14): 75% of price or Rs 1,875, whichever is less. General farmers (AGR-2) and NFSM oilseeds: 50% or Rs 1,250. Maximum 2 tarpaulins per land account. The repeat-claim rule is stated inconsistently in third-party sources.
schemes.who_benefits: Registered farmers with 7/12 land records; separate ST components.
schemes.how_suppliers_participate: No supplier empanelment or approved-vendor list was found. The farmer buys and submits the purchase bill (third-party listing). Suppliers benefit by selling through Gujarat dealers with clean GST bills in the window and by ranking for scheme searches. Verify on ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in whether bills from any seller are accepted.
schemes.window: 2025: 3-16 Feb 2025 (per sarkariyojanaguj). 2026: a social post dated 5 Apr 2026 gives 05/10/2026-15/10/2026 (unverified, possibly a date-format error); a YouTube explainer dated 31 Mar 2026 confirms a 2026 round.
schemes.relevance: Real but narrow: small tickets (2 sheets per farmer), a short 2-week window, and no supplier route found. It is worth a Gujarati explainer page and dealer push. It is not a direct B2B channel.

schemes.name: Seeds, fertiliser and tarpaulin subsidies for Adivasi farmers
schemes.what: Subsidised seeds, fertilisers, tarpaulins and other inputs for tribal farmers.
schemes.relevance: Medium: overlaps the i-Khedut ST components. Districts lie in east Gujarat.

schemes.name: Movable threshing floor (tarpaulin) subsidy, EOI for manufacturers
schemes.what: Rs 1,500 per movable threshing floor or 50% of cost, whichever is less. Ready size 8 m x 6 m, 'Multilayered, Cross laminated, U.V. Stabilized'.
schemes.how_suppliers_participate: Expression of Interest issued by the Agriculture Commissionerate, Jaipur, to empanel manufacturers. The full PDF timed out, so eligibility terms were not read.
schemes.relevance: High fit: the spec wording matches Divine's multilayer cross-laminated LDPE product. Track the next EOI.

schemes.name: Tarpaulin subsidy (Krishi department, RKVY plus state share) with supplier rate contract
schemes.what: General farmers 50% and SC/ST farmers 90% subsidy (RfP table shows Rs 1,100 per unit for general and Rs 1,980 total for SC/ST). Supplied via a tarpaulin rate contract under RfP 2022-23.
schemes.how_suppliers_participate: RfP for a rate contract issued by the agriculture department; the PDF could not be loaded, so eligibility was not read.
schemes.window: Applications invited Feb 2021 (Star of Mysore); a Kannada video of 28 Jan 2026 reports a 2026 round at 90% subsidy.
schemes.relevance: High if the specification allows LDPE multilayer; check the RfP.

schemes.name: Tarpaulins at 50% subsidy through FCI
schemes.what: State announced tarpaulins to farmers at 50% subsidy, with FCI contributing Rs 50 crore (May 2025). A Nov 2025 social post claims free tarpaulins for tenant farmers (unverified).
schemes.relevance: Medium: a large volume, likely a central tender; supplier route not found.

schemes.name: Tarpaulin distribution to tribal farmers (TSP via KVK)
schemes.what: KVK distributed tarpaulins to tribal farmers under the Tribal Sub Plan (Sep 2020).

schemes.name: GeM category: Tarpaulins made from HDPE woven fabrics as per IS 7903
schemes.what: The standard GeM tarpaulin category; bids ask for IS 7903:2017, BIS marking and HDPE woven fabric (LDPE appears only as lamination). 2026 bids: Railways 91, Army 150, Central Railway 220, Gujarat State Civil Supplies 300,660 units (est. Rs 1.13 Cr, aggregator data).
schemes.how_suppliers_participate: GeM seller registration plus a product listing to spec; MSE preferences apply.
schemes.window: Rolling; several 2026 bids closed in July 2026.
schemes.relevance: Low for Divine as-is: Divine never makes HDPE, so IS 7903 bids do not fit. Do not claim IS 7903 on the site.

schemes.name: LDPE black polythene covers for CAP (cover and plinth) grain storage
schemes.what: Annual rate contracts for black LDPE covers. Haryana DS&D: 2,000 covers at Rs 10,400 each incl. GST and freight (tender opened 15 Apr 2025; 7 bidders incl. Climax Synthetics, Vadodara; RC issued 30 Oct 2025). Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies: Rs 9,580 per cover. Punjab Food Supplies e-tender for LDPE black polythene tarpaulins (KMS 2023-24). GeM ATC for LDPE covers (2025).
schemes.who_benefits: FCI and state procurement and warehousing agencies
schemes.how_suppliers_participate: Open e-tenders and GeM bids; technical plus financial bids; a price-fall clause ties prices to the lowest supplied anywhere (Haryana proposed blacklisting over it).
schemes.window: Ahead of wheat (Apr-May) and paddy (Oct-Nov) procurement.
schemes.relevance: Medium: LDPE matches Divine's polymer. These covers are usually single-layer black film to IS 2508, so confirm a product fit first. A Gujarat firm already competes.

schemes.name: Farm pond (khet talavdi) plastic/geomembrane lining assistance
schemes.what: Government-funded geomembrane lining of farm ponds via i-Khedut (Mar 2026 report). The agriculture department lists community tanks and on-farm reservoirs with plastic/RCC lining at 75% of cost in scheduled areas.
schemes.relevance: Low-medium: market listings show liners are mostly 500-micron HDPE geomembrane, while Divine's farm-pond guide implies LDPE sheet use. Check the scheme spec before targeting it.

schemes.name: Disaster-relief reserves and relief kits (NDRF, Indian Red Cross)
schemes.what: NDRF tender for 24,000 HDPE tarpaulins with eyelets for the National Disaster Response Reserve. IRCS relief kits include tarpaulins and are procured by sealed quotations/tenders. Earlier: AP SDRF tarpaulin sheet procurement (May 2020).
schemes.relevance: Low-medium: the NDRF spec is HDPE; some kits may accept LDPE, but confirm per tender.

schemes.name: Government raincoat tenders (municipal, police, schools)
schemes.what: 361 live raincoat tenders listed in 2026 on one aggregator. MCGM tender to supply raincoats to students of its education department (winner: Super Plastic Corporation, aggregator listing). Police raincoat distributions (Bidhannagar).
schemes.relevance: Medium for ponchos if specs allow ponchos or PE raincoats; most ask for rain suits.

facts.fact: Global tarpaulin sheets market about USD 7.4 billion in 2025, 4.9% CAGR to 2036; India named the fastest-growing country at 6.4% CAGR (paid estimate, method unverified).
India tarpaulin market about USD 1.2 billion, 6.8% CAGR (base year not stated; paid estimate).
India's tarpaulin exports reach 174+ countries, with 13,041 active buyers in Volza's database (Apr 2026).
Zauba lists USD 112.9 million of tarpaulin exports at an average USD 3.23 per unit (period not stated).
Tarpaulin HSN 6306 (63061200 synthetic); EximPe states GST 18% and BCD 10% (verify the current GST rate).
GeM's standard tarpaulin category is HDPE woven to IS 7903 with BIS marking, a spec Divine (LDPE only) cannot meet.

Gujarat suppliers compete in national LDPE-cover tenders (Climax Synthetics, Vadodara, bid the Haryana 2025 RC). Ahmedabad has dense IndiaMART tarpaulin listings. No authoritative statistic on Gujarat's share of production was found.
Sector capital raising: Shakti Polytarp (Indore, tarpaulin and shade nets, brand Dinotarp) raised Rs 26.93 crore in an SME IPO in Sep 2026.
CAP storage (bag stacks on plinths under LDPE covers) is promoted by FCI as cost-effective storage, sustaining demand for LDPE covers.
Consumer raincoat search interest in Gujarat averages about 2x tarpaulin plus tadpatri combined, but it is concentrated in June-July.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Sheet tears in one season; buyers chose by colour and price
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Use-case to GSM table (farm 90-120, truck/mandi 150-200, long-term 200) with expected life and a 'why it tore' explainer.

buyer_complaints.complaint: GSM or weight shortfall (sheet lighter than claimed)
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Weight-per-sheet table for every stock size and GSM, a 'check GSM at delivery' guide (weigh, divide by area), and a stated tolerance commitment.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Price confusion: per kg vs per piece
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Show the price basis (per kg by GSM) and convert common sizes to an indicative per-sheet price; WhatsApp quote with size and GSM.

buyer_complaints.complaint: UV damage: sheet goes brittle in summer sun
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Explain UV stabilisation in Indoline layers and give expected outdoor life by GSM; avoid unverifiable 'years' claims without test data.

buyer_complaints.complaint: HDPE vs LDPE confusion; marketplaces default to HDPE/silpaulin
buyer_complaints.content_answer: An LDPE/LLDPE multilayer vs HDPE woven page: flexibility, cold-crack, folding, where each fits. State plainly that Divine does not make HDPE or IS 7903 sheets.
Cross-section photo and a plain description of the actual layers per GSM.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Eyelets tear out at ropes (trucks, sheds)
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Eyelet spacing, edge reinforcement and rope-tying guidance on truck and shed pages.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Thin disposable ponchos tear on treks
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Poncho thickness/size spec, a reusable vs disposable comparison, and a pilgrimage-use page (Kedarnath/Amarnath).

buyer_complaints.complaint: Unclear what the asterisk in 'Rs 20*' covers
buyer_complaints.content_answer: Spell out MOQ, GST, freight and colour terms next to the price.
Recyclable poncho page with the material, how it is recycled and the claim boundaries, for CSR and corporate buyers.
